title: Cross-arch tiler and fallback regression audit for FlashAttention v2/v3
creator: Ava Lin
description: Summary: This ticket is an engineering investigation and mitigation plan to reconcile cross‑architecture tiling heuristics and fallback signals between FlashAttention v2 and v3 integrations. After the v3 rollout on selected Dedicated fleets we observed intermittent token latency regressions and increased OOM fallbacks for certain long‑context workflows (>= 4k). The goal is to produce an actionable set of deterministic selector rules, add richer regression telemetry, implement a short‑term conservative fallback policy, and deliver a followup autotuner experiment.
background: What happened: Post-deploy telemetry flagged a 12–18% median tail latency regression on a subset of customer traces using long prefixes and dynamic batch mixes. Root signals point to mismatches between the runtime's tiler (microtile choices) and FlashAttention v3 kernel memory/layout assumptions when sequence length distribution is skewed. In some cases the kernel selector picks an aggressive v3 microtiling that is optimal for isolated long sequences but interacts poorly with prefill decode interleaving and KV cache memory peaks, triggering OOM fallbacks that route to slower v2 kernels.
goals: 1) Recreate regression deterministically in lab across A100/H100 and Ampere/Blackwell variants; 2) Extend kernel selector rules to include workload shape fingerprints (prefix length, decode ratio, batch heterogeneity); 3) Ship conservative runtime fallback policy to reduce production OOMs while we evaluate autotuner; 4) Add a regression dashboard and alerting for selector metric drift.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproduction harness able to trigger the latency/regression locally for at least two real customer traces on A100 and H100.
- Selector change merged that reduces OOM fallback rate by >=70% on the affected fleet in a 2‑week canary.
- New telemetry (tiler_choice, kernel_variant, prefill_peak_kv_bytes, decode_interleave_ratio) emitted and wired to runtime-tiler-dashboard.
- Autotuner experiment plan documented and scheduled as followup (ENG-61904).
decision_log:
2025-11-18: Opted to add workload fingerprinting to the selector rather than immediately rolling back v3; tradeoff: slower rollout but avoids repeated churn.
2026-01-07: Agreed on short‑term conservative fallback threshold (reserve 12% extra KV buffer for mixed prefill/decode).
2026-02-24: Decided to decouple microtiler heuristics per architecture (separate profiles for A100/H100) before final autotuner integration.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Conservative fallback reduces peak throughput for some tight latency SLAs but prevents customer-impacting OOMs.
- Per‑arch profiles increase configuration complexity and requires extra test coverage.
- Adding telemetry increases control plane billing marginally but is necessary to diagnose regressions.
work_items: Add microbench harness that runs mixed prefill+decode patterns across model sizes and seq lengths (ENG-61903.1)
Instrument runtime to emit tiler_choice and memory headroom metrics (ENG-61903.2)
Implement short-term fallback policy and canary rollout (ENG-61903.3)
Create per-arch tiler profiles and validate on H100 infra (ENG-61903.4)
Draft autotuner experiment to search tiler microtiles vs latency/cost frontier (ENG-61903.5)

2025-11-26 — Diego Morales: Added local harness to replay mixed prefill/decode interleaves. Reproduced latency tail increase at seq=4096 with batch heterogeneity >3x.
2025-12-04 — Ravi Kapoor (review): Suggested we snapshot allocator metrics (cudaMalloc retries) to correlate with kernel selection events — added to telemetry plan.

2026-01-12 — SRE (Karen Wu): Canary on Dedicated-tiler-pool-2 started; initial 48h shows OOM fallbacks reduced by ~63% after conservative policy, but median throughput decreased ~4% for small-batch requests.
2026-02-05 — Design feedback (Maya Singh): Dashboard needs a lightweight explainer for tiler_choice values to make oncall decisions faster — added legend and example traces.
2026-03-02 — Diego Morales: Per-arch profiles committed to feature branch; microbench indicates H100 benefits from larger microtiles at seq lengths >= 3k. Next: plan H100 canary.
2026-03-10 — Ava Lin: Rollout plan to Dedicated fleets prepared; will gate H100 canary on a 7‑day negative impact window and a rollback job if fallback_rate > 5%.
